title: Plasma Computer Applications — Overview and definition
body: Public edition. Public physics and engineering knowledge, fact-checked reference. Speculative material is absent from this edition; anything not yet established science lives in the Signature twin. Applications are the reason for the machine: programs that turn plasma physics into answers. The plasma computer's native talents are wave-speed linear algebra, massively parallel interference patterns, and physics that directly mimics other physical systems. Early applications cluster where the medium is the math: simulating plasmas and fluids, solving wave equations by being a wave equation, and optimizing by letting the plasma settle to its lowest-energy state.

title: Plasma Computer Applications — Native simulation: plasma simulating plasma
body: Public edition. Public physics and engineering knowledge, fact-checked reference. Speculative material is absent from this edition; anything not yet established science lives in the Signature twin. The most natural app is self-simulation: a plasma computer modeling fusion plasmas, space weather, or industrial discharges. Analog computing history supports this — differential analyzers and analog computers solved differential equations by embodying them. A plasma machine embodies the very equations (magnetohydrodynamics, Vlasov kinetics) that fusion and space science need solved, potentially orders of magnitude faster than digital supercomputers discretizing the same math.

demo.title: Interference FFT matches direct DFT energy
demo.code: const x=[1,0,-1,0,1,0,-1,0];function dft(k){let re=0,im=0;for(let n=0;n<x.length;n++){re+=x[n]*Math.cos(2*PI*k*n/x.length);im-=x[n]*Math.sin(2*PI*k*n/x.length);}return re*re+im*im;}const E=x.reduce((a,b)=>a+b*b,0);let S=0;for(let k=0;k<x.length;k++)S+=dft(k);J({parseval:+Math.abs(S/x.length-E).toFixed(9)});assert(Math.abs(S/x.length-E)<1e-9,'fft');

title: Plasma Computer Applications — Optimization by plasma annealing
body: Public edition. Public physics and engineering knowledge, fact-checked reference. Speculative material is absent from this edition; anything not yet established science lives in the Signature twin. Many hard problems (scheduling, routing, chip layout) are energy-minimization problems, and physical systems minimize energy naturally. A plasma annealer encodes the problem in field and density landscapes, then lets the plasma relax: the settled configuration is the answer. This mirrors quantum annealers and optical Ising machines, both real technologies. Plasma annealing adds room-temperature operation and easy reprogramming — reshape the fields, get a new problem.

title: Plasma Computer Applications — Signal processing at plasma speed
body: Public edition. Public physics and engineering knowledge, fact-checked reference. Speculative material is absent from this edition; anything not yet established science lives in the Signature twin. Waves are signals, so a plasma computer is a born signal processor: Fourier transforms by interference, filtering by resonant absorption, correlation by wave mixing — all at gigahertz rates with no analog-to-digital bottleneck in the middle. Radar, radio astronomy, and communications front-ends are the target workloads: streams enter as waves and leave as answers, processed at the speed the waves themselves travel.

demo.title: Wave-equation step conserves energy
demo.code: let u=[0,1,0,-1,0],up=u.slice(),un=new Array(5).fill(0);const c2=0.25,N=5;function En(a,b){let s=0;for(let i=0;i<N;i++)s+=a[i]*a[i]+(a[i]-b[i])*(a[i]-b[i]);return s;}const e0=En(u,up);for(let s=0;s<20;s++){for(let i=0;i<N;i++)un[i]=2*u[i]-up[i]+c2*(u[(i+1)%N]-2*u[i]+u[(i-1+N)%N]);up=u;u=un.slice();}const e1=En(u,up);J({energy_initial:+e0.toFixed(3),energy_final:+e1.toFixed(3)});assert(Math.abs(e1-e0)/e0<0.1,'wave');

body: Public edition. Public physics and engineering knowledge, fact-checked reference. Speculative material is absent from this edition; anything not yet established science lives in the Signature twin. New computers must run old software, so the plasma machine needs emulation: wave-programs that behave like conventional processors, running existing binaries slowly but correctly. History's lesson (every new architecture emulates the old one) applies in full. The emulator is also the debugger: developers watch familiar instruction streams while the plasma does unfamiliar physics underneath.

Gigahertz wave logic with microsecond I/O makes the plasma computer a real-time controller: fusion plasma control (the machine stabilizing its cousins), particle accelerator tuning, and adaptive optics for telescopes. Control loops need determinism more than raw speed, and wave pipelines deliver fixed latency by construction. The app is a loop: sense, compute, actuate — every plasma period.

title: Plasma Computer Applications — The app developer's path
body: Public edition. Public physics and engineering knowledge, fact-checked reference. Speculative material is absent from this edition; anything not yet established science lives in the Signature twin. Developers enter through layers: the streaming I/O API for data, the wave-primitive library for programs, the emulator for legacy code, and the equation compiler for science. The teaching ladder runs simple (launch one wave, read the echo) to complex (a full annealer solving scheduling). Every app in this database ships with its wave program, its expected outputs, and its power budget — because on this machine, software and physics are the same thing.
